ORC-1.subject: instruction-change acceptability and any verdict without a higher-rung oracle
ORC-1.mechanism: principal review at the PR checkpoint; spec consensus with exported decisions where one exists

ORC-3.subject: every commit's shape: the [ORACLE] section, the Oracle trailer, and the Token diff line on steering-text commits
ORC-3.mechanism: plugins/harness/hooks/commit-shape-gate.sh via PostToolUse on Bash; tested by tests/commit-shape-gate-test.sh

ORC-5.subject: the Token diff figure recorded on a steering-text commit
ORC-5.mechanism: re-run plugins/harness/skills/commit-protocol/scripts/token_diff.py --base <sha>^ --target <sha>; the file set derives from the commit's diff and the count_tokens endpoint is the reference

ORC-8.subject: each commit of a finished PR stack at merge time: its problem predates the branch (state, survives the merge) vs was created by the branch's own commits (journey, folded by the merger)
ORC-8.mechanism: the /merge skill runs skills/merge/scripts/classify_stack.py; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 judges each commit's message plus the ordered sibling listing against skills/merge/rubric.md; leftover fixup!/squash!/amend! subjects are folds without a model call; the merger folds on fold verdicts, may overrule (it, not the model, is the merger), and re-runs the judge on the folded stack to verify a clean landing; nothing blocks a live implementer session — the implementer's branch is a licensed scratchpad; calibration corpus and held-out error rates live in evals/stack-provenance (labels derived from the principal's recorded fold actions in mono-repo PR history)
